When a long tool/process call appears silent, do not label it hung from missing output alone. First check whether the original PID still exists, its age/CPU, descendants, and whether it has already exited; if exited, read the completed output before retrying. Never start a duplicate heavy command merely because polling returned no new lines.

observed: When AIR Commander returns EXECUTION_UNKNOWN for start_process, execution status is unknown rather than failed. Do not blindly repeat start_process. First use node registry/filesystem/process evidence to determine whether the command ran; retry only when non-execution is proven.

observed: On Windows ACCESS_DENIED replacing a tracked file is not sufficient evidence of an atomic-write code defect. Before patching write/rename logic, identify the file-handle owner with Restart Manager or equivalent read-only diagnostics. If a supervised process owns the handle, release it only through its approved lifecycle controller, then retry the original operation.
